A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same utility-maximization research despite the changed title and organization. All 16 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2 are readable, including equations, proofs, and references. Neither contains appendices, figures, or tables.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical guarantees and constructed mathematical counterexamples, but no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 remains entirely theoretical. Its additional lemmas and tightness construction are mathematical results, not empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Random-Favorites and Prior-Free-Favorites retain their procedures. However, v2 removes Iterative Random-Favorites, the explicitly defined multi-round variant proposed for future analysis in v1 Section 4.1.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or conducts training or empirical evaluation. The additional probability distributions in v2 are mathematical constructions for proofs, not added evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates comparison methods. The replacement of Vickrey-Favorites by VCG in the copies-setting counterexample is a proof revision, assessed under T1.

E3.justification: Neither version contains experimental protocols, data splits, evaluation budgets, or testing procedures. The distributions and parameter regimes describe theoretical models.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, empirical robustness tests, sensitivity experiments, or case studies. Changes to mathematical counterexamples and applicability arguments are covered under T1 and C2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experiments, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new concentration-bound reasoning in v2 is theoretical analysis, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The explicit analytical guarantee for Prior-Free-Favorites changes from E[Welfare]/[2e(1+log(n/m+1))] in v1 Section 4.2 to OptWelfare/[17.8(1+log(n/m))] in v2 Section 3.3. The logarithmic asymptotic guarantee remains unchanged. This is a revised theoretical bound, not an empirical performance change.

T1.justification: v2 Sections 3.3–3.4 substantially revise the central proofs: Lemma 2 replaces the favorites-alignment argument, Lemma 3 addresses dependence between participation counts and maximum values, and Definition 3 with Lemmas 4–5 supplies an explicit tightness reduction for both n and m. v1 instead used a short Jensen argument and directly invoked an existing lower bound. The copies-setting proof also replaces Vickrey-Favorites with VCG and explicitly relaxes the constraint on allocating bidder copies.

C1.justification: Question 1 is narrowed from approximating optimal utility for unit-demand buyers to approximating optimal welfare in the explicitly i.i.d. setting. The introduction now identifies generalization of Hartline and Roughgarden's identical-item results as the main contribution. The central constant-factor and tight logarithmic guarantees remain the same.

C2.justification: New Remarks 3–5 discuss how utility should improve with the number of items, why bidder heterogeneity can break favorites alignment, and why item copies need not provide a useful upper bound. The duality discussion changes its explanation from single-item versus multi-item problems to single-bidder versus multi-bidder problems. The main limitations concerning symmetry and welfare remain.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies implementation, hardware, runtime, code, or data-access information. v2 Definition 2 relocates and explains the single-item subroutine already specified in v1 Section 3.4; it does not disclose a new implementation procedure.

R1.justification: v2 emphasizes its relationship to Hartline and Roughgarden (2008), adds discussion of subsequent results by Ezra et al. (2024), and cites Lundy et al. (2024). The Ganesh and Hartline (2023) discussion and reference are removed. Most related-work coverage is retained.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and contribution narrative are substantially rewritten. Main results move ahead of the general-complexity discussion, while mechanism motivation and definitions are regrouped with their analysis. This substantially changes the reading order and exposition beyond simply inserting new proofs.

P2.justification: Both PDFs retain the same single-column text-and-equation presentation and contain no figures or tables. Pagination changes follow the expanded and reorganized text rather than a substantive visual-layout redesign.

improvement.justification: v1 invokes a lower bound without establishing its transfer from identical items to i.i.d. heterogeneous items and leaves dependence unaddressed in its short Jensen argument. v2 Sections 3.3.1 and 3.4 supply a dedicated dependence analysis and an explicit tightness construction with utility and welfare comparison lemmas. These substantially improve the completeness and checkability of the central argument, supported by clearer organization. The explicit approximation constant becomes more conservative, but the asymptotic guarantees are retained.
